title: Final: under the hood
sub: Awaiter, state machine, allocations and ExecutionContext
cards/0/task: Walk the state machine in both modes: with waiting and with ready results.
cards/1/q: What does the state field hold?
cards/1/options/0: The number of the await where the method stopped
cards/1/explain: The switch in MoveNext uses it to jump to the right spot.
cards/2/explain: Subscribe to completion, then get the result.
cards/3/q: Which of these methods, finishing without a single pause, allocates nothing on the heap?
cards/3/options/2: Any async method: no pause means no allocations
cards/3/explain: ValueTask<int> keeps the result inside the struct. async Task<int> creates a new Task<int> for 1000: ready-made tasks exist only for a few values.
cards/4/q: Which are true? Select all that apply.
cards/4/options/0: AsyncLocal survives a thread switch after await
cards/4/options/1: The builder calls SetException on an exception
cards/4/options/2: A ValueTask can be awaited many times
cards/4/explain: A ValueTask is single-use: you can await it exactly once.
cards/5/q: A handler called SumAsync(), and the first task inside isn't ready yet. At what point does the handler get the Task?
cards/5/options/0: When the first MoveNext reached the unfinished await, subscribed and returned
cards/5/options/1: Immediately on the call, before the method's first line runs
cards/5/explain: builder.Start runs the first MoveNext synchronously, and only after it returns does the method return builder.Task.
cards/6/q: The life of an async method with one await
cards/6/items/0: MoveNext #1 (from builder.Start) runs up to the await
cards/6/items/1: The awaiter isn't ready: state is saved and MoveNext is subscribed to the task's completion
cards/6/items/2: The task completes and MoveNext #2 is called
cards/6/items/3: GetResult and the rest of the method
cards/7/pairs/0/1: The method body, cut at each await
cards/7/pairs/1/1: The key that makes any type awaitable
